topics.title: Vectors and Resultant Forces
topics.subject: physics
outcomes: understand the differences between vector and scalar quantities, and give examples of each (u)
understand that a number of forces acting on a body can be represented by a single resultant force (u, s)

body.text: A scalar quantity has only a size (magnitude) — for example mass, distance, speed, and time. A vector quantity has both a size and a direction — for example weight, displacement, velocity, and force.

When two or more forces act on an object at the same time, they can be combined into a single resultant force that has the same overall effect on the object. If two forces act at an angle to each other (not simply in line), the resultant can be found using a scale drawing, placing the force vectors head-to-tail, or using Pythagoras' theorem when the forces are perpendicular to each other.
Use the PhET Vector Addition simulation below. Add vectors together and see how their resultant depends on both their sizes and their directions.
